Maintenance Report — MNT-0067-001

Asset: WELL-0067 (SW-24 Well 067, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 04 Nov 2022 08:00 · Finished: 04 Nov 2022 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0067-0003 on 2022-11-03 Report written: 06 Nov 2022

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0067-0003 at 12:00 on 2022-11-03 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.4% of the pad area, estimated 4.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.6 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 228 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 182 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 4.0 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0067-001 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.86% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0067-004

Asset: WELL-0067 (SW-24 Well 067, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 28 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 03 May 2023 16:00 · Well stopped for this job: 128 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0067-0028 on 2023-04-27 Report written: 04 May 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0067-0028 showed the wellhead at 27.2 °C with the air at 27.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Asset: WELL-0067 (SW-24 Well 067, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 09 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 03 Sep 2025 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 593 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0067-0145 on 2025-08-07 Report written: 03 Sep 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0067-0145 showed the wellhead at 32.5 °C with the air at 32.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.
